source_uncertainties: Frame extracted (not in the 30-s frame set): l9Ol7qsyRCg at 68 s, the Module 03 'Source' slide, shown 64-71 s; it names Pope, Turbulent Flows (Cambridge University Press, 2000). Kept in _editorial/tmp, not in the repository.

Unverified (named in reader text as slide-caption attributions, not opened; Journal of Fluid Mechanics papers behind a paywall on 2026-10-05): Tong and Warhaft (1995), the centreline velocity record (f0004); Hussein, Capp and George (1994), J. Fluid Mech. 258, 31-75, the mean jet profile at Re = 95,500 (f0016). The reader text now says each paper was not available and that the values are read from the slide. The running-case nozzle (25 mm, 56 m/s) is a teaching construction and is not claimed to be the apparatus of either experiment.

Values read from a slide figure (f0004): trace between about 1.5 and 6 m/s, mean about 3.4 m/s. The slide's '25 %' does not state whether it is the r.m.s. value; the running case takes it as r.m.s. and says so.

Slide error corrected (f0025): lambda = 1e-9 m is labelled both 'average spacing between molecules' and 'mean free path'. U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 Table 10 gives mean free path 6.6328e-8 m and number density 2.5470e25 m^-3 (spacing 3.4e-9 m). The chapter states both and shows that Kn << 1 holds with either value.
Slide wording (f0028, eq. 10-11): S_ij as defined includes the isotropic part; it is 'deviatoric' only when div U = 0. The chapter states the condition.

Handwritten sign (zKfqomYsmRs f0021; transcript L16 ~525-535 s): the expansion of curl(omega x U) carries '+U(div omega)'; the identity has '-U(div omega)'. The term vanishes, so eq. (6.18) is unaffected; the chapter uses the correct identity.

Spoken claim not adopted: 'there is no 2D turbulence' / 'turbulence does not exist in 2D' (L16 ~688 s and ~799 s). The slide (f0004) says 2D turbulence is 'vastly different'; the chapter attributes both and follows Boffetta and Ecke (2012, pp. 428, 430).

Spoken slip corrected by the lecturer (L16 ~650-750 s): nu*lap(omega) first called the vortex-stretching term, then corrected to omega.grad U. Spoken slip corrected by the lecturer (L15 ~904-947 s): the sign of grad p in the momentum equation.

Lecture usage: the handwriting on OjW3S1VSadk f0050 labels reacting species mass fraction an 'active scalar'. The chapter separates 'conserved' (no source) from 'passive' (no feedback on U) and attributes the lecture's usage.

Spoken statement attributed, not verified: the usual solution procedure (solve momentum with an assumed pressure, correct the pressure with the Poisson equation), L15 ~1229-1241 s. A primary source for projection methods (Chorin 1968, Math. Comp.) could not be downloaded (publisher challenge page on 2026-10-05) and is not cited.
Not treated: the choice of pressure boundary condition in a bounded domain that keeps div U = 0 on the boundary; the chapter says so.

Air properties: the chapter uses U.S. Standard Atmosphere sea-level values (288.15 K, nu = 1.4607e-5 m^2/s); chapter 5 used the lecture value nu = 1.5e-5 m^2/s (2.7 % larger). Stated in the model section.

ASR spellings corrected (slide text and standard spelling): 'Tong and Wahhab' = Tong and Warhaft; 'Osbourn-Rollinger experiment' = Osborne Reynolds's experiment; 'quantity equation' = continuity equation; 'index rotation' = index notation; 'new' = nu; 'a row' = a rho; 'special derivative' = spatial derivative; 'hatred variables' = hatted variables.
Timestamps are section anchors from local speech-recognition segment times; they locate topic changes to within a few seconds.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.lecture_material: None (the slides' jet records motivate the choice of a jet).
sections.research_extension: U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976, Table 10, p. 20: sea-level rho, mu, nu, c.
sections.teaching_construction: Formal model (continuum, constant density, Newtonian, conserved passive scalar); running case of one air jet at the nozzle (25 mm, 56 m/s, Re = 9.6e4) and at a downstream station (8 m/s, u0 = 2 m/s, ell0 = 0.1 m, eta = 79 micrometres).

sections.section: A turbulent velocity signal and its smooth mean
sections.lecture_material: Centreline U1(t) record (Tong and Warhaft 1995 per caption), 25 % fluctuations, not periodic, wide range of time scales, 'stable'; mean profile at Re = 95,500 (Hussein, Capp, George 1994 per caption), smooth, close to laminar shape; enhanced mixing; Re = UL/nu.
sections.teaching_construction: Framing question (which equations govern U(x,t)); deterministic equations versus irregular solutions; definition of the mean by pointer to chapter 7.

sections.section: The continuum hypothesis and the two descriptions of a flow
sections.lecture_material: Continuum hypothesis, Kn = lambda/l << 1 with lambda = 1e-9 m and l = 1e-4 m; Eulerian and Lagrangian fields (X+, Y, rho+, U+); material derivative; material points, lines, surfaces, volumes; no mass flux across a material surface.
sections.research_extension: U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976: mean-free-path definition (section 1.3.8, eq. 47, p. 17) and sea-level mean free path 6.6328e-8 m and number density 2.5470e25 m^-3 (Table 10, p. 20).
sections.teaching_construction: Correction of the slide value (spacing 3.4e-9 m versus mean free path 6.6e-8 m); Kn at the Kolmogorov scale of the running case (8.4e-4); chain-rule derivation of D/Dt; probe example.

sections.section: Conservation of mass and the incompressible approximation
sections.lecture_material: Continuity equation (slide eq. 1); material and specific-volume forms (slide eq. 2); incompressible flow gives div U = 0 (solenoidal); incompressibility defined as density independent of pressure.
sections.research_extension: Speed of sound 340.29 m/s (U.S. Standard Atmosphere Table 10).
sections.teaching_construction: Reading of div U as fractional volume rate; D rho/Dt = 0 versus rho constant; low-Mach estimate |div U| ~ Ma^2 U/L and drho/rho ~ Ma^2/2; running-case values 1.4 % (nozzle) and 3.5e-5 (station).

sections.section: Momentum, the Newtonian stress and the Navier-Stokes equations
sections.lecture_material: Newton's second law; surface and body forces; symmetric stress tensor; momentum equation (slide eq. 3); Newtonian stress split into isotropic and deviatoric parts (slide eq. 4).
sections.teaching_construction: Trace of the viscous stress is 2 mu div U (deviatoric only when div U = 0).

sections.section: Momentum, the Newtonian stress and the Navier-Stokes equations (continued)
sections.lecture_material: Substitution of the stress into the momentum equation using continuity; incompressible Navier-Stokes equations (slide eq. 5); impermeability and no-slip conditions; Euler equations; Euler solutions differ from vanishing-viscosity NS solutions; Euler equations still used.
sections.teaching_construction: Index derivation showing where continuity enters; four equations for four unknowns; backward link to chapter 5's singular-perturbation section.

sections.section: Pressure is fixed by the constraint of zero divergence
sections.lecture_material: Pressure acts like a body force with no connection to density; four equations, four unknowns, no pressure equation; divergence of momentum gives the Poisson equation (slide eq. 6); Poisson equation necessary and sufficient for a solenoidal field to remain solenoidal; solution procedure (assume p, correct by Poisson).
sections.teaching_construction: Evolution equation for div U (6.11) and the necessity/sufficiency argument with its two conditions; wall Neumann condition (6.13); free-space Green's-function solution and non-locality (6.14); magnitude p ~ rho u0^2 = 4.9 Pa. Uniqueness in the sufficiency argument taken from the maximum principle (6.16) with Gamma = nu.

sections.section: Conserved passive scalars and their bounds
sections.lecture_material: Conserved passive scalar equation (slide eq. 7); temperature and mixture fraction, thermal and mass diffusivity; boundedness phi_min <= phi <= phi_max; passive (temperature) versus active (reacting species) in the lecture's usage; summary of the equation set.
sections.teaching_construction: Separation of 'conserved' and 'passive'; heated-jet example (5 K, 1.7 % density change); maximum-principle statement (6.16) for a bounded region or periodic box, with continuity on the closed region, proof and conditions; conservative versus advective form; pointer to the discrete counterexample (exercise 3).

sections.section: The vorticity equation and vortex stretching
sections.lecture_material: Vorticity as curl of U (slide eq. 8); turbulence is rotational; curl of NS with the vector identity for the convective term (slide eq. 9); pressure term vanishes; vortex stretching stretches material lines aligned with omega; stretching vanishes in 2D; 2D turbulence vastly different from 3D (slide).
sections.research_extension: Boffetta and Ecke 2012: 2D turbulence never strictly realized but approximates large-scale atmosphere and oceans (p. 428); enstrophy bound dZ/dt = -2 nu P, energy dissipation vanishes as nu -> 0, inverse energy cascade, contrast with 3D vortex stretching (p. 430).
sections.teaching_construction: Baroclinic term shown to vanish only for constant density; material-line equation (6.19) and the Cauchy-type correspondence for nu = 0; enstrophy equation (6.20); 2D enstrophy bound (6.21) derived; running-case vorticity ratio 117.

sections.lecture_material: Decomposition of the velocity gradient (slide eq. 10); S_ij and Omega_ij (slide eqs. 11-12); tau_ij = -p delta_ij + 2 mu S_ij, viscous stress independent of rotation; omega_i = -eps_ijk Omega_jk (slide eq. 13); Omega_ij a tensor, omega_i not.
sections.research_extension: Hunt, Wray and Moin 1988 (p. 196, eqs. 2.1-2.2): II = du_i/dx_j du_j/dx_i = E_ij^2 - omega_i^2/2; eddy zones where II < -II_E, plus a pressure-minimum criterion.
sections.teaching_construction: Sign check of (6.24) and its inverse; pseudovector argument with det(a); (omega.grad)U = S omega and the stretching/tilting split; Poisson right side as S:S - |omega|^2/2 (6.26) with rigid-rotation and plane-strain limit checks; box-average balance (6.27) and eps = nu <omega'^2> for homogeneous fluctuations; running-case rms vorticity 2.3e3 1/s.

sections.lecture_material: Transformation-properties figure; two experiments with different time, place, orientation, platform, fluid and scale; scaling with U0 (script U) and L0 (script L); scaled continuity, momentum and Poisson equations (slide eq. 14); Re the only parameter; identical scaled fields for equal Re and identical ICs and BCs; scaled Euler equations scale invariant.
sections.teaching_construction: Scaled pressure and the scalar's 1/(Re Sc); three boundaries (model approximations, identical scaled data, statistics for turbulent flows); half-scale air model at Ma = 0.33.

sections.section: Invariance under changes of frame and time reversal
sections.lecture_material: Translation (slide eq. 15); rotation and reflection with direction cosines (slide eq. 16); time reversal changes the sign of the viscous term, Euler invariant (slide eq. 17); Galilean invariance (slide eq. 18).
sections.teaching_construction: Chain-rule proof of Galilean invariance (6.31); accelerating frame absorbed into pressure; derivation of the rotating-frame equation (6.32) from the rotation of frame-fixed vectors, with Coriolis and centrifugal terms; link to chapter 5's Coriolis parameter; Table 6.1.

sections.section: Executable check of the identities and of the pressure equation
sections.teaching_construction: NumPy spectral program on a periodic box: random solenoidal field; checks of div U, (6.24), (6.25), (6.26), (6.27); divergence tendency with Poisson pressure and with p = 0; Taylor-Green exact pressure; 2D versus 3D stretching; failure test without the projection.

sections.section: What the equations assume and what they do not establish
sections.research_extension: Boffetta and Ecke 2012, p. 428 (2D never strictly realized).
sections.teaching_construction: List of the four approximations with their running-case error measures; status of each derived result; pointers to chapters 7, 8, 9. Closing statement of what the reader can now do.

sections.lecture_material: Exercise 6 uses the time-reversal transformation of the slides. Exercises 7-10 are adapted from the course practice problems L57-P1 (7UyTD2lT0sI 1:41), L58-P5 (nBZWHP4w8fY 6:08), L58-P6 (nBZWHP4w8fY 21:57) and T1-P2 (fgMG7Jd89pw 15:44), which are one problem in Exercise 9, and T1-P1 (fgMG7Jd89pw 0:54), as assigned by _editorial/practice-map.md.
sections.research_extension: Exercise 2 uses the Standard Atmosphere values.
sections.teaching_construction: Six original exercises (derive and check a limit, compute and check assumptions, counterexample, derive, design, judge a claim) and four adapted practice-problem exercises (index form of the compressible momentum equation, projection step and pressure Poisson equation, enstrophy equation, four suffix-notation identities), with full solutions for all ten.

Table 10, 'Sea-level values of atmospheric properties': C_s,0 = 3.40294e2 m/s; L_0 = 6.6328e-8 m; N_0 = 2.5470e25 m^-3; T_0 = 2.8815e2 K; eta_0 (kinematic viscosity) = 1.4607e-5 m^2/s; mu_0 = 1.7894e-5 kg/(m s); rho_0 = 1.2250 kg/m^3.
references.page_checked: p. 17 (PDF p. 33); p. 20 (PDF p. 36); scanned pages rendered and read

references.title: Hunt, Wray, Moin 1988, Eddies, streams, and convergence zones in turbulent flows (CTR Proceedings of the Summer Program 1988, pp. 193-208)
references.supports: Eq. (2.1b): 'II = (du_i/dx_j)(du_j/dx_i) = E_ij^2 - (1/2) omega_i^2', E_ij the symmetric strain tensor; criterion (a) II < -II_E for eddy zones ('the irrotational straining is small compared with the vorticity'); criterion (b) a pressure minimum in the zone, eq. (2.2).
references.page_checked: p. 196 (PDF p. 4); page image rendered and read

references.title: Boffetta and Ecke 2012, Two-dimensional turbulence (Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 44, 427-451)
references.supports: p. 428: 2D turbulence 'is never realized in nature or in the laboratory'; 'large-scale motions in the atmosphere and oceans are described, to first approximation, as 2D turbulent fluids'; the review is devoted to 'stationary, forced-dissipated, 2D turbulence'. p. 430: eq. (6) dZ/dt = -2 nu P; 'Because Equation 6 bounds enstrophy from above, Equation 5 implies that eps_nu -> 0 as nu -> 0. This is the main difference with respect to 3D turbulence in which Z can be amplified by vortex stretching ... resulting in finite energy dissipation in the limit of vanishing viscosity'; energy 'transferred to large scales by the inverse cascade'.
references.page_checked: p. 428 (PDF p. 2); p. 430 (PDF p. 4); course copy at courses.physics.ucsd.edu
